questions: How many days are there in a leap year?
A leap year adds February 29, giving 366 days instead of 365.
Which colour do you get by mixing blue and yellow paint?
In subtractive (paint) colour mixing, blue and yellow combine to make green.
How many sides does a hexagon have?
The prefix hexa- means six; a hexagon is a six-sided polygon.
What is the largest ocean on Earth?
The Pacific covers roughly a third of Earth's surface, more than any other ocean.
How many minutes are in one hour?
An hour is divided into 60 minutes, a legacy of Babylonian base-60 counting.
Which instrument has 88 keys in its standard modern form?
A standard modern piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.
What is the freezing point of pure water at sea level in degrees Celsius?
Pure water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F) at standard atmospheric pressure.
How many continents are commonly recognised in the seven-continent model?
The seven-continent model lists Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and South America.
What do bees produce from flower nectar?
Honey bees convert nectar into honey by enzymatic action and evaporation.
Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
Iron oxide (rust) on its surface gives Mars its reddish appearance.
How many letters are in the modern English alphabet?
The modern English alphabet has 26 letters, from A to Z.
A triangle is a polygon with three edges and three vertices.
Which month has the fewest days in the Gregorian calendar?
February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year.
What is the main language spoken in Brazil?
Brazil was colonised by Portugal, and Portuguese is its official language.
How many legs does a spider have?
Spiders are arachnids and have eight legs, unlike six-legged insects.
What is the opposite of 'north' on a compass?
North and south are opposite cardinal directions.
Which gas do humans need to breathe in to survive?
Human cells use oxygen for aerobic respiration.
What is the tallest animal on land?
Giraffes can exceed 5 metres in height, taller than any other land animal.
How many hours are in a day?
A day is divided into 24 hours.
Which of these is a primary colour of light in the RGB model?
The RGB model uses red, green and blue as its additive primaries.
What is the hardest naturally occurring mineral?
Diamond scores 10, the maximum, on the Mohs hardness scale.
How many strings does a standard violin have?
A violin has four strings tuned G, D, A and E.
What is the capital city of Canada?
Ottawa, in Ontario, has been Canada's capital since before Confederation in 1867.
Which element has the chemical symbol 'Fe'?
Fe comes from the Latin word for iron, ferrum.
In which country would you find the ancient city of Petra?
Petra, carved into rose-red sandstone, is in southern Jordan.
How many players are on the field for one team in a standard soccer match?
Each association football team fields 11 players, including the goalkeeper.
What is the longest bone in the human body?
The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in the body.
Which language has the most native speakers worldwide?
Mandarin has the largest number of first-language speakers of any language.
What is a group of lions called?
Lions live in social groups called prides.
Which unit is used to measure electrical resistance?
Resistance is measured in ohms, named after Georg Ohm.
What is the smallest prime number?
2 is the smallest prime and the only even prime; 1 is not prime.
Which famous clock tower bell in London is nicknamed Big Ben?
The Great Bell of the Palace of Westminster
The bell of St Paul's Cathedral
Big Ben is the nickname of the Great Bell in the Elizabeth Tower at the Palace of Westminster.
How many degrees are in a right angle?
A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees, a quarter turn.
Which currency is used in Japan?
The Japanese yen is Japan's official currency.
What is the name for a word that reads the same backwards and forwards, like 'level'?
A palindrome reads the same in both directions.
What colour is the 'black box' flight recorder on most aircraft actually painted?
Flight recorders are painted bright orange to make them easier to find after an accident.
Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
The heart is a muscular pump that circulates blood through the blood vessels.
In which city is the Colosseum located?
The Colosseum is an ancient amphitheatre in the centre of Rome.
How many zeros are in one million?
One million is written 1,000,000, with six zeros.
Which is the only letter that does not appear in the name of any U.S. state?
Every letter except Q appears in at least one U.S. state name.
What is the term for a baby kangaroo?
Young kangaroos and other marsupials are called joeys.
What does the 'www' in a web address stand for?
WWW is short for World Wide Web, invented by Tim Berners-Lee.
Which of these countries is landlocked?
Switzerland has no coastline; it is surrounded by France, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein and Italy.
What is the boiling point of pure water at sea level in degrees Fahrenheit?
Water boils at 212 °F, equivalent to 100 °C, at standard pressure.
What is the only continent with no permanent human population?
Antarctica hosts research stations but has no permanent residents.
Which country has the most time zones when overseas territories are included?
Counting its overseas territories, France spans 12 time zones, more than any other country.
What is the name of the fear of long words, itself a famously long word?
Hippopotomonstrosesquippedaliophobia is an ironic, informal name for a fear of long words.
In Morse code, what letter is represented by a single dot?
E, the most common English letter, is a single dot; T is a single dash.
Which planet has a day longer than its year?
Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once but only about 225 to orbit the Sun.
What is the most widely spoken language in South America by number of countries where it is official?
Spanish is official in nine South American countries; Portuguese is official only in Brazil.
What is the standard number of squares on a chessboard?
A chessboard is an 8 × 8 grid of 64 squares.
What is the traditional collective noun for a group of crows?
'A murder of crows' is the traditional term; 'a parliament' is used for owls.
In what year did the first humans land on the Moon?
Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
What is the national animal of Scotland?
The unicorn has been Scotland's national animal since the 14th century and appears on its royal arms.
How many bones are in the adult human body?
A typical adult skeleton has 206 bones; infants have more that later fuse.
Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
The statue was a gift from the people of France, dedicated in 1886.
What is the longest river in Europe?
The Volga, flowing through Russia to the Caspian Sea, is about 3,530 km long.
Which number is represented by the Roman numeral 'XL'?
X before L subtracts ten from fifty, giving 40.
What does the acronym 'NATO' stand for?
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, founded in 1949.
What is the smallest country in the world by area?
Vatican City covers about 0.49 km², making it the world's smallest sovereign state.
Which vitamin is produced by human skin when exposed to sunlight?
UVB light converts a cholesterol derivative in the skin into vitamin D3.
How many hearts does an octopus have?
An octopus has two branchial hearts and one systemic heart.
What is the name of the line of latitude at 0 degrees?
The Equator is the 0° line of latitude; the Prime Meridian is 0° longitude.
